AN ACT to consolidate with amendments the Lands Clauses Act 1871, the Public
Authorities Acquisition of Land Acts 1923 to 1948 and other enactments relating
to the acquisition of land by public authorities and others; and for connected
purposes.
GENERAL NOTE: References to the Commissioners are to be construed in accordance
with the Church Act 1992 s 2(4).
PART I – APPLICATION OF ACT
1 Application of Act
(1) Where by virtue of any enactment (whenever passed) any person or
body of persons, whether corporate or unincorporate, may acquire land
compulsorily, the provisions of this Act shall apply to the acquisition,
subject to such exceptions, adaptations and modifications (if any) as may
be specified in that enactment.
(2) Where by virtue of an Act of Parliament having effect in the Island any
person or body corporate is authorised to acquire land compulsorily for
the purposes of any public undertaking, the provisions of Part III shall
apply to such acquisition.
(3) Where any question of disputed compensation or other matter is by any
enactment to be determined in accordance with Part III, that Part shall
apply, with any necessary modifications, to that question or matter as it
applies to a question or dispute which is under this Act to be determined
in accordance with section 3.
c AT 9 of 1984 Page 7

Section 2 Acquisition of Land Act 1984
PART II – AUTHORISATION PROCEDURE
2 Procedure for authorising compulsory purchase
(1) Subject to this section, an authority possessing compulsory powers may
be authorised to acquire land compulsorily by a resolution of Tynwald
and not otherwise.
(2) An authority possessing compulsory powers shall, not less than 21 days
before applying to Tynwald for authorisation under subsection (1), give
notice in writing of its intention so to do to each person of full age
interested in any land proposed to be acquired —
(a) describing the land;
(b) stating the purpose for which it is required; and
(c) naming a place where a plan of the land may be inspected free of
charge at all reasonable hours.
(3) Where any person interested in such land is under legal disability, notice
under subsection (2) may be given to the person having the control and
management of the property of that person; and if there is no such
person, notice under subsection (2) may be given to a suitable person
appointed, with the consent of the High Court, by the authority to
represent that person.
(4) Notice of the hearing of the petition to Tynwald shall be given in at least
two newspapers published and circulating in the Island, and such notice
shall contain the particulars specified in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of
subsection (2).
PART III – ASSESSMENT OF COMPENSATION
Arbitration
3 Tribunal for assessing compensation
(1) Where any land is authorised to be acquired compulsorily —
(a) any question of disputed compensation; and
(b) any other question or dispute which is authorised by this Act to
be determined in accordance with this section;
shall be referred to and determined by the arbitration of such one of the
panel of official arbitrators appointed under this section as may be
selected by the Governor.
(2) The Governor may, in consultation with the Treasury, appoint such
number of persons as he thinks fit, being persons with special knowledge
Page 8 AT 9 of 1984 c

Acquisition of Land Act 1984 Section 4
in the valuation of land, to act as official arbitrators for the purposes of
this Act.1
(3) A person appointed under subsection (2) shall hold office for such term
as the Governor may before such appointment determine.
(4) There shall be paid such fees, salaries or remuneration of official
arbitrators so appointed as the Treasury, with the approval of Tynwald,
may determine.2
(5) An official arbitrator to whom any question is referred under this section
is in this Act referred to as “the arbitrator”.
4 Reference to agreed arbitrator
(1) Nothing in this Act prevents the reference of any question or dispute, if
the parties so agree, to an arbitrator agreed between the parties.
(2) Where a question is referred to an arbitrator under subsection (1), this
Part (except sections 3 and 9(2), (7) and (10)) shall apply as if the
arbitration were under section 3.
Assessment
5 Rules for assessing compensation
(1) Compensation in respect of any compulsory acquisition shall be assessed
in accordance with the following rules:
(1) The value of land shall, subject as hereinafter provided, be taken to
be the amount which the land if sold in the open market by a willing
seller might be expected to realise, with an addition of 10 per cent. on
account of the acquisition being compulsory:
(2) The special suitability or adaptability of the land for any purpose
shall not be taken into account if that purpose is a purpose to which it
could be applied only in pursuance of statutory powers, or for which
there is no market apart from the requirements of any authority
possessing compulsory purchase powers:
(3) Where the value of the land is increased by reason of the use thereof
or of any premises thereon in a manner which could be restrained by
any court, or is contrary to law, or is detrimental to the health of the
occupants of the premises or to the public health, the amount of that
increase shall not be taken into account:
(4) Where land is, and but for the compulsory acquisition would
continue to be, devoted to a purpose of such a nature that there is no
general demand or market for land for that purpose, the
compensation may, if the arbitrator is satisfied that reinstatement in
some other place is bona fide intended, be assessed on the basis of the
reasonable cost of equivalent reinstatement:
c AT 9 of 1984 Page 9

Section 6 Acquisition of Land Act 1984
(5) The provisions of rule (1) shall not affect the assessment of

ACQUISITION OF LAND (ARBITRATION) RULES 19841
Made: 19 July 1984
Coming into Operation: 15 August 1984
In exercise of the powers conferred on the Governor in Council by section 9(8), (9) and
(10) of the Acquisition of Land 19841, and of all other enabling powers, the following
Rules are hereby made :-
1 Citation, commencement and interpretation
(1) These Rules may be cited as the Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules
1984 and shall come into operation on the 15th August 1984.
(2) In these Rules –
“the Act” means the Acquisition of Land Act 1984;
“the arbitrator”, in relation to any question or dispute, means –
(a) such one of the official panel of arbitrators appointed under section
3 of the Act as is selected by the Governor to determine the question
or dispute under subsection (1) of that section; or
(b) where the question or dispute is referred under section 4(1) of the
Act, the arbitrator agreed between the parties.
2 Application to references under s. 4(1) of the Act
The following provisions of these Rules shall not apply to an arbitration under
section 4(1) of the Act, namely rules 3; 4, 6, 7, 9, 17 and 30.
3 Notice of reference
(1) Proceedings for the determination of a reference may be instituted by a
person entitled under any enactment to do so, or (if there is no such
person) by any person who wishes the reference to be determined, sending
to the Government Secretary a notice of reference in the form set out in the
1 1984 c.1
c GC No.1984/0170 Page 1

Rule 4 Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984
Schedule, together with sufficient copies for service upon every other
party to the reference.
(2) The notice of reference sent to the Government Secretary shall be
accompanied –
(i) where the question is one of compensation payable on the
compulsory acquisition of land, by a copy of the notice to
treat (if such notice has been served) and of any notice of
claim and any amendment thereof delivered to the
acquiring authority in pursuance of section 10(1)(b) of the
Act;
(ii) in any other case, by a copy of the order, direction, notice,
decision, authorisation or other document in consequence of
which proceedings for the determination of the reference
are instituted.
(3) A notice of reference relating to the assessment of compensation on the
compulsory acquisition of land shall not be given before the expiration of
28 days from the date of service of the notice to treat or (where no notice
to treat is served) of the notice of claim.
4 Entry of reference
(1) Upon receiving a notice of reference the Government Secretary shall enter
particulars of the reference in a register kept for the purpose and shall send
a copy of the notice to every party to the reference (other than the party
instituting the reference).
(2) The Government Secretary shall transmit the notice of reference to the
Governor for him to select one of the official panel of arbitrators appointed
under section 3 of the Act to determine the reference.
(3) The Government Secretary shall notify each. party to the reference of the
name and address of the arbitrator.
5 Sittings of Tribunal
(1) The arbitrator shall sit at such place in the Island as he may from time to
time determine.
(2) The arbitrator shall send to each party to a reference a notice informing
him of the place and date of the hearing which, unless the parties
otherwise agree, shall not be earlier than 14 days after the date on which
the notice is sent.
(3) Any person to whom notice has been sent under paragraph (2) may apply
to the arbitrator in accordance with rule 15 for an alteration of the place or
date of the hearing.
Page 2 GC No.1984/0170 c

Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984 Rule 6
6 Public sittings
The arbitrator shall sit in public unless he is determining a reference without a
hearing in accordance with Rule 7.
7 Contested proceedings without hearing
(1) Notwithstanding rule 10 as to oral evidence and rule 14, but subject to
paragraph (2), the arbitrator shall have power to determine any reference
without an oral hearing and any party to the reference may apply to the
arbitrator in accordance with rule 15 for an order that the reference shall
be so determined.
(2) An order shall not be made under this rule in respect of any proceedings
relating to the amount of compensation –
(i) which is payable in respect of the compulsory acquisition of
land; or
(ii) which depends directly or indirectly on the value of any
land.
(3) After an order has been made under this rule the arbitrator may, of his
own motion or on the application of any party to the reference, require any
party to the reference to furnish to the arbitrator such statements of case,
or reply thereto, or further and better particulars thereof, as the arbitrator
may specify.
(4) After an order has been made under this rule any party to the reference
may submit in writing to the arbitrator any representations which he
wishes the arbitrator to take into consideration.
(5) Any statements, replies or particulars required by virtue of paragraph (3)
and any representations made by any party, and any document or other
Information required to be delivered by any party to any reference in
accordance with rule 11, shall be sent to the arbitrator together with
sufficient copies of the same for all the other parties to the reference, within
28 days of the order or requirement (as the case may be).
(6) The arbitrator shall, within 7 days of receiving by virtue of this rule any
statements, replies, particulars, representations, document or other
information, send to every other party to the reference a copy of the same.
(7) If, after having received a copy of any statements, replies, particulars,
representations, document or information under paragraph (6) any party
to the reference wishes to make any representations to the arbitrator he
may submit the same in writing to the arbitrator within 28 days of the
receipt by him of the said copy, and paragraphs (5) and (6) shall apply to
such representations; but no party to any reference shall make any
representations on more than one occasion in the reference except by the
leave of the arbitrator.

of witnesses and the hearing of evidence were references to
representations.
(9) The arbitrator may at any time and for any reason order that proceedings
which he. was in the process of deciding without an oral hearing shall be
heard and may thereupon give directions for the disposal of those
proceedings in accordance with these rules.
(10) Rules 21 and 22 shall not apply to any reference to which this rule applies.
8 View of land
(1) Subject to paragraph (2), the arbitrator may inspect the land which is the
subject of the reference.
(2) When the arbitrator intends to enter on any premises in pursuance of
paragraph (1) he shall give notice to the parties of that intention and the
parties shall be entitled to attend the inspection.
(3) This rule shall apply, so far as practicable, to any comparable land to
which the attention of the arbitrator is directed as they apply to the land
which is the subject of the reference.
9 Proceedings to be consolidated or heard together
(1) Where two or more notices of reference have been given in respect of
several interests in the same land in dispute, an application may be made
by any party to the references that the references be heard together.
(2) Where any such notices of reference as are referred to in paragraph (1)
have been given, the arbitrator may, without any application in that
behalf, order that the references be consolidated or heard together.
(3) An order may be made with respect to some only of the matters to which
the notices of reference relate.
10 Evidence
(1) Evidence before the arbitrator may be given orally or, if the parties to the
reference consent or the arbitrator so orders, by affidavit, but the arbitrator
may at any stage of the proceedings make an order requiring the personal
attendance of any deponent for examination and cross-examination.
(2) Rule 15 shall apply to an application to the arbitrator for leave to give
evidence by affidavit.
(3) Nothing in the Evidence Act 19832, or in rules of court made under it, shall
prevent expert evidence from being adduced before the arbitrator by any
2 1983 c.7
Page 4 GC No.1984/0170 c

Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984 Rule 11
party notwithstanding that no application has been made to the arbitrator
for a direction as to the disclosure of that evidence to any other party to
the reference.
11 Power to order discovery,. etc.
(1) The arbitrator may on the application of any party to the reference or of
his own motion order any party –
(a) to deliver to the arbitrator any document or other Information
which he may require and which it is in the power of the party to
deliver;
(b) to afford to every other party to the proceedings an opportunity to
inspect those documents (or copies of them) and to take copies;
(c) to deliver to the arbitrator an affidavit or make a list stating
whether any document or class of document specified or described
in the order or application is, or has at any time been in his
possession, custody or power, and stating when he parted with it;
(d) to deliver to the arbitrator a statement in the form of a pleading
setting out further and better particulars of the grounds on which
he intends to rely and any relevant facts or contentions;
(e) to answer interrogatories on affidavit relating to any matter at issue
between the applicant and the other party; or
(f) to deliver to the arbitrator a statement of agreed facts, facts in
dispute and the issue or issues to be tried by the arbitrator.
Provided that nothing in this rule shall be deemed to require any
information to be disclosed contrary to the public interest.
(2) Where an order is made under paragraph (1) in the case of proceedings
other than those to which rule 7(5) applies, the arbitrator may give
directions as to the time within which any document Is to be sent to the
arbitrator (being at least 14 days from the date of the direction) and the
parties to whom copies of the document are to be sent.
(3) Rule 15 shall apply to this rule as appropriate to applications and in
relation to cases where the arbitrator acts of his own motion.
12 Failure to supply documents
If it appears to the arbitrator that any party to a reference has failed to send a copy
of any document required under these Rules to be sent to any other party or to
the arbitrator, the arbitrator may direct that a copy of the document shall be sent
as may be necessary and that the further hearing of the proceedings be adjourned,
and may in any such case require the party at fault to pay any additional costs
occasioned thereby.
c GC No.1984/0170 Page 5

Rule 13 Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984
13 Expert witnesses
(1) An application for leave to call more than one, or more than one
additional, expert witness may be made to the arbitrator in accordance
with rule 15 or at the hearing.
(2) Where more than one party intends to call an expert witness, every such
party shall, within 28 days after being so requested by the arbitrator, send
to the arbitrator a copy of each of the following documents relating to the
evidence to be given by the expert witness, together with sufficient copies
for service upon the other parties –
(i) every plan and valuation of the land which is the subject of
the reference (including particulars and computations in
support of the valuation) which it is proposed to put in
evidence;
(ii) either a statement of any prices, costs or other particulars
and any plans relating to a property or properties other than
that land which are proposed to be given in evidence in
support or plans will be relied upon.
(3) The arbitrator shall, within 7 days after receiving all the documents
required to be supplied by the parties under paragraph (2), send to each
party copies of the documents supplied by the other party.
(4) If an application for leave to call more than one, or more than one
additional, expert witness is made at the hearing and is granted by the
arbitrator, or if at the hearing any party seeks to rely upon any plans,
valuations or particulars, which have not been sent to the arbitrator in
accordance with this rule, the arbitrator may adjourn the hearing on such
terms as to costs or otherwise as he thinks fit.
14 Right of audience
In any proceedings, a party may appear and be heard in person, by an advocate
or, on obtaining leave of the arbitrator, by any other person.
15 Interlocutory applications
(1) An application for directions of an interlocutory nature in connection with
any reference shall be made in writing and shall state the grounds upon
which the application is made.
(2) If the application is made with the consent of all parties it shall be
accompanied by consents signed by or on behalf of the parties.
(3) If the application is not made with the consent of every party, then, before
it is made, a copy shall be served on every other party and the application
shall state that this has been done.
Page 6 GC No.1984/0170 c

Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984 Rule 16
(4) A party who objects to the application may, within 7 days after service of
a copy on him, send written notice of objection to the arbitrator and to the
applicant, and before making an order on the application the arbitrator
shall consider all the objections which he has received and, If any party
wishes to appear before him, the arbitrator shall give him and every other
party an opportunity to do so.
(5) In dealing with an application under this rule, the arbitrator shall have
regard to the convenience of the parties and the desirability of limiting so
far as practicable the costs of the proceedings and shall communicate his
decision in writing to every party.
16 Pre-trial review
(1) The arbitrator may on the application of a party to a reference or of his
own motion order a pre-trial review to be held on a day, being not less
than 14 days after the making of the order unless the parties to the
proceedings agree otherwise, and the arbitrator shall send to each party to
the proceedings a notice informing him of the time and place of the pre-
trial review.
(2) On the pre-trial review the arbitrator shall give all such directions as
appear necessary or desirable for securing the just, expeditious and
economical disposal of the reference.
(3) The arbitrator shall endeavour on the pre-trial review to secure that the
parties make all such admissions and agreements as ought reasonably to
be made by them in relation to the reference and may record in the order
made on the review any admission or agreement so made or any refusal
to make any admission or agreement.
(4) Where any party seeks a specific direction, he shall, so far as practicable,
apply for such direction on the pre-trial review and shall give to the
arbitrator and every other party notice of his intention to do so, and if an
application which might have been made on the review is made
subsequently the applicant shall pay the costs of and occasioned by the
application, unless the arbitrator is of the opinion that there was sufficient
reason for the application not having been made on the review.
(5) Rule 15 shall have effect as if the pre-trial review were the hearing of an
interlocutory application and accordingly the arbitrator may, on the
review, exercise any of the powers exercisable on an interlocutory
application and may do so of his own motion.
(6) If any party does not appear on the pre-trial' review the arbitrator, after
giving the parties an opportunity to be heard, may make such order as
may be appropriate for the purpose of expediting or disposing of the
proceedings.
c GC No.1984/0170 Page 7

Rule 17 Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984
17 Certificates of value
An application for a certificate of value under section 11 of the Act shall be made
in writing to the Government Secretary, and the party by whom the application
is made shall provide the arbitrator on his request with such information as may
be required to enable the certificate to be given.
18 Extension of time
The time appointed by or under these Rules for doing any act or taking any steps
In connection with any proceedings may be extended, on an application to the
arbitrator in accordance with rule 15, upon such terms (if any) as the justice of the
case may require, and an extension may be ordered although the application is
not made until after the expiration of the time appointed.
19 Sealed offers
An unconditional offer of any sum, or of readiness to accept any sum, as
compensation shall not be disclosed to the arbitrator until it has decided the
amount of compensation to be awarded to the party to or by whom the offer was
made, but a copy of the offer enclosed in a sealed cover may be sent to the
arbitrator or delivered to him at the hearing by the party who made the offer and
shall be opened by the arbitrator after he has decided the amount of the
compensation.
20 Withdrawal or dismissal or reference etc., before hearing
(1) A reference may be withdrawn by sending to the arbitrator a written
notice of withdrawal signed by all parties to the proceedings or by their
advocates or agents.
(2) An applicant may, at any time before the hearing of the references apply
to the arbitrator for an order to dismiss the proceedings, and the arbitrator
may thereupon make such order as may be just.
(3) Rule 15(2), (3) and (4) shall apply to an application under paragraph (2).
(4) Where any party has failed to pursue any reference with due diligence or
has failed to comply with any of these Rules, the arbitrator may, after
giving the parties an opportunity to be heard, make an order that the
proceedings be heard by the arbitrator or make such other order as may
be appropriate for the purpose of expediting or disposing of the
proceedings.
21 Procedure at hearing
(1) Unless the arbitrator otherwise directs a party claiming compensation or
a party to whom any rent or rent charge requiring to be apportioned is
payable shall begin and, in any other case, the party by whom the
reference was instituted shall begin.
Page 8 GC No.1984/0170 c

Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984 Rule 22
(2) Subject to the provisions of these Rules the procedure at the hearing of any
reference shalt be such as the arbitrator may direct.
22 Default of appearance at hearing
If any party to a reference does not appear at the time and place appointed, the
arbitrator may hear and determine the reference in his absence and may make
such order as to costs as he thinks fit:
Provided that, where proceedings have been dismissed or determined under this
rule in the absence of a party, the arbitrator may, on an application made by that
party within 7 days of the dismissal or determination, if he is satisfied that that
party had sufficient reason for his absence, set aside the dismissal or
determination on such terms as to costs or otherwise as he thinks fit.
23 Decision of arbitrator
(1) The decision of the arbitrator on a reference shall be given in writing,
together with a statement of the arbitrator's reasons for his decision:
Provided that the arbitrator may give his decision and his reasons orally
in cases where he is satisfied that no injustice or inconvenience to the
parties would be occasioned by his doing so.
(2) Where an amount awarded or value determined by the arbitrator is
dependent upon the decision of the arbitrator on a question of law which
is in dispute in the reference, the arbitrator shall ascertain, and shall state
in his decision, the alternative amount or value (if any) which he would
have awarded or determined if he had decided otherwise on the question
of law.
(3) The arbitrator shall send a copy of the decision (or, where the decision was
given orally, a statement of its effect) to the Government Secretary and to
every party who has appeared before him.
(4) If any directions are given by the High Court for the amendment of any
decision of the arbitrator on which a case has been stated for the decision
of the Court, the amendments shall be made by the arbitrator accordingly
and he shall send copies of the amended decision to every person who was
notified of the original decision in accordance with paragraph (3).
24 Consent orders
Where the parties to any reference have agreed upon the terms of any orders to
be made by the arbitrator, particulars of the terms, signed by all the parties or by
their advocates or agents, shall be sent to the arbitrator, and an order may be
made by the arbitrator in accordance with those terms in the absence of the
parties.
c GC No.1984/0170 Page 9

Rule 25 Acquisition of Land (Arbitration) Rules 1984
25 Costs
(1) Except in cases to which section 10(1), (2) or (3) of the Act applies, the costs
of and incidental to any reference shall be in the discretion of the
arbitrator.
(2) If the arbitrator directs that the costs of a party to the reference shall be
paid by any other party, the arbitrator may settle the amount of the costs
by fixing a lump sum, or he may direct that the costs shall be taxed by the
Chief Registrar.
26 Service of notices
Any notice or other document required or authorised to be served on any person
for the purpose of these Rules shall be deemed to have been duly served if sent
by pre-paid post to that person at his ordinary address or to his address for
service specified in any notice given under these Rules; and any notice or other
document required or authorised to be sent to the arbitrator shall be sent to him
at the address notified to the parties under rule 4(3).
27 Change of address
A party to any reference may at any time by notice in writing to the arbitrator and
to every other party to the reference change his address for service under these
Rules.
28 Substituted service
If any person to whom any notice or other document is required to be sent for the
purpose of these Rules cannot be found, or has died and has no personal
representative, or is out of the Island, or if for any other reason service upon him
cannot be readily effected in accordance with these Rules, the arbitrator may
dispense with service upon that person or may make an order for substituted
service upon such other person or in such other form (whether by advertisement
in a newspaper or otherwise).
29 Failure to comply with Rules
Any failure on the part of any person to comply with the provisions of these Rules
shall not render the reference or anything done in pursuance thereof invalid,
unless the arbitration so directs.
30 Fees
(1) Fees shall be paid by cheque or postal order, drawn in favour of the
Government Treasurer.
(2) The reference fee shall be payable by the party by whom the proceedings
were instituted (without prejudice to his right to recover the amount of the
Page 10 GC No.1984/0170 c

fee from any other party by virtue of any order as to costs) on sending his
notice of reference to the Government Secretary.
(3) The hearing fee and the amount of any expenses payable to the arbitrator
shall be payable by such of the parties as the arbitrator may direct (without
prejudice as aforesaid).

HOME LOSS PAYMENTS REGULATIONS 20001
Approved by Tynwald: 11 July 2000
Coming into Operation: 1 August 2000
In exercise of the powers conferred on the Treasury by section 23B(4) of the Acquisition
of Land Act 19841 , and of all other enabling powers, the following Regulations are
hereby made:—
1 Citation, commencement and interpretation
(1) These Regulations may be cited as the Home Loss Payments Regulations
2000 and, subject to section 23B(5) of the Act, shall come into operation on
the 1st August 2000.
(2) In these Regulations, “the Act” means the Acquisition of Land Act 1984.
2 Claim for home loss payment or discretionary payment
No home loss payment or discretionary payment shall be made except on a claim
in writing made by the claimant giving such particulars as the acquiring authority
may reasonably require for the purpose of determining whether the payment
should be made and, if so, its amount.
3 Making of home loss payment
Where a person is entitled to a home loss payment, the payment shall be made
on or before the later of the following dates —
(a) the date of displacement;
(b) the last day of the period of 3 months beginning with the making
of the claim.
4 Claim by 2 or more persons in respect of same dwelling
Where there are 2 or more persons entitled to make a claim to a home loss
payment in respect of the same dwelling (whether by virtue of joint occupation
1 1984 c.9
c SD No.2000/0401 Page 1

Regulation 5 Home Loss Payments Regulations 2000
or regulation 4) the payment to be made on each claim shall be equal to the whole
amount of the home loss payment divided by the number of such persons.
5 Claim by person residing in different dwellings in same building
Where the claimant has successively been in occupation of or resided in different
dwellings in the same building, being dwellings consisting of a room or rooms
not constructed or structurally adapted for use as a separate dwelling, section
23A(1) of the Act and regulation 4 shall have effect as if those dwellings were the
same dwelling.
6 Claim where potential claimant has died
Where a person (“the deceased”) entitled to a home loss payment dies without
having claimed it, a claim to the payment may be made, by any person, not being
a minor, who —
(a) throughout a period of not less than one year ending with the date
of displacement of the deceased, has resided in the dwelling, or a
substantial part of it, as his only or main residence; and
(b) is entitled to benefit by virtue of testamentary dispositions taking
effect on, or the law of intestate succession or the right of
survivorship between joint tenants as applied to, the death of the
deceased.

Preamble
Whereas by a Clause in the before-mentioned Act of Settlement, the respective
Tennants and Inhabittants of the said Isle are obliged to pay (besides their Rents
and Fines therein expressed and mentioned) all other Dues, Duties, and
Carriages, as have been formerly accustomed; and that the fixing and
ascertaining of the said Carriages is by the said Act left to the Consideration of a
Tynwald Court;
1 Duties and Carriages payable to Lord
That the Tennants and Inhabittants of this Isle shall pay and do their Carriages
to the Lord as formerly accustomed; that is to say, four Carriages from every
Quarter of Land, and one Carriage from every Cottage and Intackholder within
the said Isle; and the same to be performed either by the Labour of Horses, or
Service of Men, as the Governor shall thing fitt to order, and hath been formerly
accustomed; and that these Carriages shall be taken for the Lord’s Use as his
Lordship or the Governor for the Time being shall think fit to employ them; and
that no Tennant shall be exempt from doing of these Carriages but such as have
been already legally accustomed to be freed thereof.

2 All lettings for longer than 5 years by way of security to be deemed

And whereas by another Clause in the afforesaid Act of Settlement, all Persons
who then had mortgaged, or should thereafter mortgage, all or any Part of
Messuages, Lands, Tenements, Milns, Cottages, Intacks, or other
Heridittaments, unto any person, and should not actually redeem the same to
his own proper Use within the Space of five Years next after the
Commencement of the said Mortgage, should be looked upon as an alienation,
and the Mortgagee admitted as Tennant to the same in such Manner and on
such Terms as in and by the said Clause is fully mentioned and expressed: And
forasmuch as it is conceived that severall fraudulent Bargains may be made for
letting of Lands, Tenements, Milns, Cottages, Intacks, and other
Heredittaments, for the Security of Money, under other Notions than that of
Mortgage, to defraud our Honourable Lord of a Fine; be it therefore ordered,
ordained, and enacted by the Authority aforesaid, That all such Bargaines as
shall hereafter be made and given for the Security of any Sum of Money upon

And also whereas by another Clause in the said Act of Settlement, it is
mentioned and expressed that all Intacks and Cottages, as had been taken out of

Nusances) should be referred to the Consideration of a Tynwald Court to
